Daemon 93958, commit 46106685eee34a73cb26223d05cb2199c40b715b, process start 2026-11-20T07:29:23.641880Z. First reading was more than ten minutes after start. Stable PID/commit/stamped start identity across all four readings and the sample.

Actual window: 2026-11-20T07:39:41.491034+00:00 to 2026-11-20T07:44:49.023794+00:00, 307.532 seconds, not the scheduled 240 seconds: the fourth reading was late during sample analysis. The measured window is retained; nothing was recaptured.

Total completions: 3699, 12.0280/s. Inbox contributes 91.0233% of recorded non-park handler time. The single refused registration has high mean latency but negligible volume. Mean-latency rank alone is not a CPU-cost ranking.

Launches: recorded daemon total is 506 at every reading, zero delta at every by_op site. One canonical `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` window began 07:41:17.245Z: 285.0 new PIDs/s machine-wide, sampled 239.8/s. Readable command lower bounds include git 28.8/s, git-ai 17.2/s and a test-binary name pij_daemon-5fab 16.5/s; these do not prove owners or successful exec. No new daemon child was attributed by the sampler; that is a lower bound, while the daemon's recorded spawn counters stayed flat.

One authorized sample, 07:42:03.277Z for 30 s, same identity, completed successfully. The machine sampler and stack diagnostic overlap the middle interval; do not treat that interval's rise as causal route evidence. Non-wait frontier total is 2,240 after excluding 403,932 blocked/parked weights, including daemon-log socket reads, control reader, idle workqueue and SQLite busy sleeps. SQLite busy-sleep weight is 537 (sqliteDefaultBusyCallback → unixSleep → __semwait_signal), excluded from the work denominator.

These percentages are SAMPLE OCCUPANCY WEIGHTS, never CPU percentages. Generic HTTP wrapper ancestry is not proof of instrumentation overhead. SQLite is the largest named work family, but its sqlx worker stacks do not identify originating request routes. Native inbox frames are present, and pane-observer/background/runtime work is also present. This does not establish that inbox owns the shared SQLite CPU, nor explain the historical 22.5%. F231/F222 diagnosis remains OPEN.

Ranked candidates: GET /v1/inbox first, POST /v1/whoami second, POST /v1/inbox/heartbeat third. Next measurement (owner approval required; not executed): a fixed-cohort native idle-inbox workload sweep against an isolated real SQLite fixture, holding database shape and WHOAMI/heartbeat traffic constant, measuring process/worker CPU against waiting-cohort size. This tests the leading inbox-polling hypothesis without assuming wall time is CPU; separate route-origin/background SQL tracing if the sweep does not resolve attribution.
